options.content: **Developer tier.** Every panel here needs the exporter started with `--include-engula-debug-metrics` (off by default). If the panels are empty, check that flag before anything else.

panels.title: Zip Tasks
panels.description: Compression task flow, from the user tier. `Attempted` minus `Created` is what never became a task. `Inline urgent` is the queue being full at creation, `Inline main thread` is the io threads not draining it afterwards.

panels.title: Rezip Tasks
panels.description: Recompression task flow. Rezip has no inline-urgent path — a full queue gates creation instead, so `Created` is already the queued count.

panels.title: Queue Lengths
panels.description: Work pending in the two compression queues. The shared completion queues are on the Engula Scheduler dashboard.

panels.title: Rezip Hit Rate
panels.description: `Created / Attempted` for rezip. Its `Attempted` ticks on the 100ms cron whether or not there is anything to recompress, so having nothing to do is the normal state — read this hit rate rather than reading `Attempted` as workload.

panels.title: Current Line Sizes
panels.description: Compressed lines grouped by how much of a zip batch their original record bytes fill (ec_calc_nsize_bucket_id_by_size: size * 10 / EA_ZIP_BATCH_SIZE, so 10% per bucket with the last one a catch-all). Lines below 50% are the ones rezip will not bother re-dictionarying.

panels.title: Line Sizes Over Time
panels.description: The same distribution over time, stacked.

panels.title: Rezip Candidate Pool
panels.description: Lines split at the threshold rezip actually uses: EC_REZIP_BUCKET_THRESHOLD is EC_DICT_BUCKET_COUNT / 2, so a line whose original bytes already fill 50% or more of a zip batch is never re-dictionaried. An empty candidate pool is why rezip finds no work.

panels.title: Line Population
panels.description: Lines held back from compression (`Skipped`) against lines queued for reclamation (`Recycling`).

panels.title: Line Churn
panels.description: Compressed lines created against lines deleted. Creation outrunning deletion for long stretches means the line population is growing.

panels.title: Dictionary Count
panels.description: Compression dictionaries currently held.

panels.title: Dictionary Cost
panels.description: Memory the dictionaries occupy, in total and averaged per dictionary. This is the overhead compression pays for itself.

panels.title: Dictionaries Deleting
panels.description: Dictionaries queued for asynchronous deletion but not yet gone.

panels.title: Dictionary Deletion Rate
panels.description: Dictionaries actually reclaimed by the async deleter.

panels.title: Zip Blocks
panels.description: Blocks consumed and written back by compression passes.

panels.title: Zip Block Bytes
panels.description: Bytes consumed and written back by compression passes, at block level. These are the user-tier `engula_zip_{retired,produced}_bytes_total`; the record-level detail next to it stays in the developer tier.

panels.title: Zip Records
panels.description: Records read out of the old blocks and written into the compressed ones. A lasting gap means records are being dropped along the way.

panels.title: Zip Record Bytes
panels.description: The same records measured in bytes — compression's effect at record level, before block-level packing.

panels.title: Rezip Blocks
panels.description: Blocks consumed and written back by recompression passes.

panels.title: Rezip Block Bytes
panels.description: Recompression at block level, from the user-tier `engula_rezip_{retired,produced}_bytes_total`.

panels.title: Rezip Records
panels.description: Records moved through recompression.

panels.title: Rezip Record Bytes
panels.description: Recompression measured in bytes at record level.

panels.title: Block Compression Ratio
panels.description: Block bytes written back as a fraction of block bytes consumed. This is the codec and the repacking together — read it against Record Compression Ratio, whose difference from this is what packing contributes. Lower is better.

panels.title: Record Compression Ratio
panels.description: Record bytes written back as a fraction of record bytes consumed — the codec's effect on its own, before blocks are repacked. A record ratio close to the block ratio means packing is contributing nothing on top of the codec.

panels.title: Line Count Reconciliation
panels.description: `Live` counts the lines the gauges report; `Created − deleted` counts them from the lifetime counters. The two must track: ec.h states created − deleted is what stands behind the live gauges. A drift between them is a counting bug, not a workload change — the ec_destroy path bypassing ec_delete_line() was exactly this.

panels.title: Records Conservation
panels.description: Records into a pass minus records out of it. Compression rewrites records, it does not drop them, so both lines belong at zero. A sustained departure means records are being lost or double-counted on that path.

panels.title: Encode Errors
panels.description: Compression encode failures. This should sit flat at zero; anything else needs looking at.

title: Engula Compression
description: Developer-tier view of Engula's compression: the zip and rezip task flow, how lines and dictionaries are sized and recycled, what each pass gives back, and two invariants that catch counting bugs. Requires the exporter to run with --include-engula-debug-metrics.
